sectionsUsed: Create your first test: a test_*.py file with a function whose name starts with test and a plain assert; run pytest and read the failure report
Assert that a certain exception is raised: with pytest.raises(...)
Asserting with the assert statement: pytest shows the values of subexpressions such as function calls on failure
Assertions about expected exceptions: pytest.raises as a context manager
Calling pytest through python -m pytest: also adds the current directory to sys.path
Specifying which tests to run: node ids such as test_mod.py::test_func
Possible exit codes: 0 all passed, 1 some tests failed
Requesting fixtures: a test names a @pytest.fixture function as a parameter, and pytest passes in its return value
@pytest.mark.parametrize: argument names as a comma-separated string and a list of value tuples; the test function takes those names as parameters and runs once per tuple
pytest: helps you write better programs; detailed info on failing assert statements; auto-discovery of test modules and functions
